title: I rebuilt the residents in my city-builder, so naturally I made them do a fashion show
author: Kiko_Production
selftext:
I’ve been working on a pretty big overhaul of the residents in my indie city-builder, City Paradise (Godot 4.5, C#).  
And since I needed to test all the new outfits and hairstyles anyway, I decided to organize a little fashion show, complete with a runway, an audience, and three very serious judges from the game’s story.

I completely rebuilt the residents around a shared low-poly body with just 612 triangles and 22 bones. The old skeleton had 65 bones, including 43 for fingers… despite everyone having mitten hands.  
I’ve also made a modular clothing system with 71 clothing pieces, 27 hats, customizable colors, seasonal outfits, and uniforms for different jobs. A fully dressed resident now uses around 1,400–1,500 triangles instead of 4,458. There are also new hairstyles and shader-based faces with 12 different expressions.

I’ve been experimenting with an AI-assisted workflow. I start with my own character references, use ChatGPT to generate concept sheets, and Tripo to turn them into rough 3D models. Claude Code then helps me write Blender scripts to simplify the meshes, fit everything onto the characters, and get it working in Godot.  
There’s still a lot of trial and error involved, and most parts go through several iterations before I’m happy with how they look in-game.  
The fashion show itself actually runs inside the game, with seven cameras recording

I’m thinking about adding some fun pop-culture-inspired residents and little Easter eggs. Maybe someone with Teto-like look, or other recognizable characters reimagined in the game’s style.  
I’d love to hear your ideas! Who would you like to see walking around City Paradise?
